findings.title: A single `pending-review` status across four boundaries hides which review is owed
findings.description:
The architecture's goal of "First-class status representation" (240-arch, Design Goals) says runners should act on the status "without parsing recommendation strings". In this design, all four boundaries produce the same `pending-review` / `review-failed` statuses. The `NextAction` type does not change (TD-7), and the review type (`arch`/`slice`/`tasks`/`code`) appears only in the free-text `rationale`. A runner that needs to start the right review agent would have to parse that string.

The status also replaces the lifecycle status that was there before (`needs-tasks`, `in-implementation`, `complete`). So `getStatus()` consumers, like the visualizer, can no longer see where the slice is in its lifecycle.

Fix: return the review type in a structured way without changing the `NextAction` shape. Either add an optional additive field, or use a defined machine-readable field already on `SliceStatus`/`enrich()`. Name that field in "Provides to Other Slices" so Amoeba and Squadron have a contract.

findings.title: The pre-slice-plan (`arch`) boundary has no defined owner or index
Parse failures can't be told apart from a missing verdict, which the architecture requires
findings.description:
240-arch, Technical Considerations ("File-read failure modes") says: "The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The design calls `parseFrontmatter` swallowing errors "exactly the behavior the gate needs". The data flow (line 161) reads only `.data.verdict`, so a malformed, unreadable or permission-denied file looks the same as a valid file with no `verdict`. The TD-7 rationale templates have no parse-failure wording, and the failure isn't logged anywhere.

The routing is correct (both cases go to `UNKNOWN` and then to `unknownAs`). Only the required, observable signal is missing. Fix: use the `found` flag `parseFrontmatter` already returns. Have `found: false` on an existing file produce a rationale that names the parse failure, plus a warning in the `enrich()` warnings. Add a test that checks for that signal.

findings.title: Leaving `review_type` keys set but unread ignores user config without telling them
findings.description:
TD-4 keeps `workflow.review_gates.*.review_type` defined but unread. A user who sets `review_gates.pre_advance.review_type = "slice"` gets no error, and the gate looks for `code` anyway. This conflicts with the architecture's "Fail-fast on configuration errors" principle (an "unrecognized per-gate config is a config error … not a silent pass or silent block") and the project's rule against silent fallbacks.

The stated reason for keeping the keys (not breaking an existing `.context-forge.toml`) can be met without silence. Fix: either remove the keys, or keep them and add a warning to `NextAction.warnings` (or reject them in `validate`) when one is non-empty. Also, the parenthetical deferring this choice to implementation leaves the decision the slice plan gave to this design partly open. State the choice.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/241-slice.gate-logic-in-workflownavigator.md#TD-4: reviewType is position-derived — the 240 per-gate `review_type` keys become inert

findings.title: Mapping from boundary to per-gate threshold key, and the `resolveGateConfig` signature, are inconsistent
findings.description:
`resolveGateConfig(config)` is said to resolve "the boundary-specific threshold", but it doesn't take a `Boundary` parameter. The design names boundaries in camelCase (`preAdvance`, `preSlicePlan`). The keys shipped by 240 use snake_case (`workflow.review_gates.pre_advance.threshold`; see 240-slice:268-275). Nothing defines how one becomes the other, so the code would have to build key names from strings or keep a second table that isn't mentioned.

Fix: add the boundary parameter (`resolveGateConfig(config, boundary)`). Then either put the config-key segment in the `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE` record or add a sibling constant, so each boundary is defined in one place.

findings.title: Per-boundary trigger for pre-implementation fires mid-implementation
findings.description: "Task file exists, not complete" covers both zero boxes checked and partly checked. A slice that's halfway through implementation with no `tasks` review would switch from `in-implementation` to `pending-review`. That may be the intent (the review was owed before work started), but the design should say so explicitly and include it in the per-boundary test. Only the current boundary is evaluated, so a `complete` slice with a passing code review and no slice/tasks review will advance. That also deserves one sentence so nobody reads it as a bug.

findings.title: Deferral target 910 has no document yet
findings.description: `interfaces: [..., 910]` and TD-6 send the ~50-site `STATUS` cleanup to maintenance slice 910. No `910-*` document exists under `project-documents/user/`. The slice plan does mention 910, so this is in scope, but the cleanup has nowhere to be tracked until 910 is planned.
